item.title: Miles McBride may have played his way out of New York
item.author: Russell Richardson
item.content:encoded: Miles “Deuce” McBride arrived in New York as the 36th pick in the 2021 draft, a short-ish, square-jawed defender with a shaky jump shot. The inconsistent three-ball never worried Tom Thibodeau. The grizzled skipper loved watching a 6’2” guard stalk ballhandlers the length of the court, the basketball equivalent of a German shepherd harassing a cockapoo.Eventually, the offense came around. Deuce put in plenty of reps with Westchester, waited behind veteran guards on the MSG depth chart and spent marathon hours in the gym rebuilding his jumper. His three-point shooting went from his greatest liability to one of his greatest strengths, rising from 25% on 1.7 attempts per game as a rookie to 41% on 6.6 attempts during the championship season. His playing time increased accordingly. Although still primarily a reserve, he went from nine minutes per game to 26.When RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley were traded to the Raptors, Leon Rose’s next order of business was locking down the promising McBride, who had so far been buried on the bench. On the day of the trade, December 30, 2023, the former West Virginia Mountaineer, then 23, agreed to a three-year, $13 million fully guaranteed contract extension. The front-loaded deal began the following season and runs through 2026–27, with his salary decreasing each year.Deuce significantly outperformed it. He stepped into a larger rotation role, improved his efficiency, contributed as a two-way guard and posted career highs in points, minutes and assists. He became a reliable sparkplug off the bench and an occasional starter (43 so far). Better still, his contract provided the Knicks with roster flexibility under the league’s salary-cap and apron restrictions. Recent estimates have placed his market value at $10 million to $12 million per year, if not higher, while his actual cap hits remained remarkably low: approximately $4.7 million in 2024–25, $4.3 million in 2025–26 and less than $4 million in 2026–27.McBride further proved his value during the championship run, playing through lingering pain after February hernia surgery sidelined him for roughly two months. He described the sensation as “like someone stabbing your groin, hip and ab at the same time,” yet still played anyway.Now all that wonderful success may carry Deuce out of New York. Stefan Bondy reports in the that McBride, Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart are eligible for extensions and remain unsigned. McBride’s situation is the most eyebrow-raising of the three. He did not sign before the August 11 soft deadline, after which an extension would prevent the Knicks from trading him during the season. Bondy considers a new deal unlikely and highlights McBride as perhaps the Knicks’ best expendable trade asset.McBride has a favorable expiring contract, and the Knicks have more guards than available minutes. They also have needs that may become more urgent as the season unfolds. New York acquired Andre Drummond to back up Towns, but Drummond is on the other side of 30, with considerable mileage after a career spent wrestling NBA bigs. If Rose & Co. decide they need another center or a different kind of rotation player, they have limited ways to make a meaningful midseason move. Trading Deuce may provide the cleanest path.With Mitchell Robinson gone, McBride is the longest-tenured Knick. He is also among the few remaining players whom the organization drafted and developed. When done well, player development creates value, and the best proof of that value is when another team craves what you produced. Which teams might be interested? Off the top of the dome: the Hornets, Grizzlies, Clippers, Nets, and Suns. If none of them has a big man the Knicks want, we already know Leon is capable of roping in a third team that does.Nobody in the P&T bullpen wants to see Deuce go. He fits the exact profile of a player we love: gritty, team-first, defensively minded, willing to play through pain, and committed to improving year after year. Ideally, that kind of player remains a Knick for life, followed by a chair at MSG Network or a front-office position. But who knows what the Knicks’ situation at center will be around the midseason trade deadline? If this is Deuce’s last ride, let’s appreciate it.

Friday Posted & Toasted Notes: King JB, Tacko Tuesday, GM KD
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: I thought I had a ton of content to include in the notes, then realized there were just a handful of bullet points to it, so I needed to wait a few days to pad it further. Maybe we’re not so close to the new season as I initially thought.Mayor Zohran Mamdani has his own answer to the “King of New York” debate.Jalen Brunson, however, wants absolutely no part of that.“Imagine I get on this call with you, right? I’m like, ‘Yo, no king of New York’s here,’ whatever, whatever. You guys are going to look like, ‘What the f**k, this dude is so self-centered.’”NYP’s Stefan Bondy believes Josh Hart and the Knicks remain on track to stay together long term, even if an extension does not happen immediately. He thinks, however, Karl-Anthony Towns’ next contract could become one of the Knicks’ biggest financial decisions. Meanwhile, Bondy sees Deuce McBride as an increasingly likely trade asset.Jalen Brunson already has an eye on life after basketball.“I would coach high school or the pros. I would not want to coach college.”Julius Randle says he has no bitterness about watching the Knicks win a championship after his departure. Never stop liking Jules, fellas.Miles McBride brought the Larry O’Brien Trophy back to his old high school community. Deuuuuuuuuce!!!Jose Alvarado is aiming significantly higher than simply remaining a useful Knicks reserve, hunting for that 6MOY award next season.“I still haven’t done what I wanted to do with my career. I got a lot of goals that I want to push for and this is probably going to be the most hard-working summer I probably put in. I want to be in the conversation of Sixth Man of the Year one day. Obviously I got to work, obviously situations where the minutes, consistency and stuff like that is always going to be a problem because I know I’m never going to pass the eye test. If you look at me, I’m not the most tallest, most athletic to the NBA world. So I just know going into a room, I got to be the most out-working person, hardest-working person and the rest will take care of itself.”The Knicks are still looking for a third center, and SI’s Joseph Randazzo floated Chris Boucher as a possible veteran option.Believe it or not, OG Anunoby is headed to network television.Jordan Clarkson has apparently been officially friend-zoned by Bebe Rexha. In a busy week for JC, he also crossed paths with rising tennis star Alex Eala at the U.S. Open, with the two bonding over their Filipino heritage.Kevin Durant has a clear post-playing-career ambition already in mind: running Team USA.

item.title: Tour of Britain Men: Olav Kooij turns the tables on Tim Merlier to win stage 3
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: Olav Kooij (Decathlon CMA CGM) sprinted to victory on stage 3 of the Tour of Britain Men, overcoming rival Tim Merlier (Soudal-QuickStep) in the final metres to take his first victory in this edition of the race.Merlier settled for second in Beverly in what ended up feeling like a two-man sprint, with the two head and shoulders above the rest of the field. Axel Källberg (Lucky Sport Cycling Team) took third."It’s always nice to get a win, especially after yesterday to try and really do my sprint at the right moment," Kooij said. "With the headwind I really had to wait for the moment that I could find my way through."I think also in the end, the way we controlled, the boys got me into the final in a really perfect way. I’m really happy to take the win."Tarteletto-Isorex's Yorben Lauryssen went on a big solo attack 48km from the finish, but just fell short of a spectacular surprise win when he was caught with 6.5km to go by the surging sprint trains.It was a messy final kilometre with teams battling to get organised, and Soudal-QuickStep looked to have the best lead-out, but Kooij managed to come from a boxed-in position to speed around the Belgian and claim the win.Race leader and stage 1 winner Lewis Askey (NSN) finished safely in the bunch in 17th to retain the leader's jersey for another day, but there may be some frustration in the NSN camp, as Ethan Vernon was on the receiving end of quite a cut-off from Merlier in the sprint, and had to settle for seventh.Stage 3 from Hull to Beverley was another sprint-friendly day with a finish on circuits, though there were three small climbs to deal with along the way: Burton Road, Tire Ewe Hill and Keepers Hill.A six-rider break got away early in the stage, made up of King of the Mountains Michael Schuran (Team United Shipping), Dylan Vandenstorme (Flanders-Baloise), Karl Hall (Hucare Factory Team), Victor Johannsen (BHS-PL Beton Bornholm) and the Tarteletto-Isorex duo of Arne Santy and Gianni Marchand.They were allowed to build a two-minute gap and have their day out, but the sprint teams were keeping them close enough to catch. They stayed away over the first two climbs, where Schuran extended his KOM lead, but were caught by the peloton over the final climb.The attacks resumed quickly after that, though, with Lauryssen setting off and building a two-minute gap, with Conn McDunphy (APS Pro Cycling by Team Cadence Cyclery) chasing behind him.Lauryssen put in an impressive ride to maintain a 1:30 gap into the final 20km, but he had the full force of the peloton and sprinters chasing behind him. He fought valiantly on the final laps, but was swept up with 6.5km to go as the sprint teams ramped up to speed.It was UAE Team Emirates-XRG who took up the pacing as the catch was made, trying to split things up in the wind since they don't have a pure sprinter in this race, but they couldn't make the difference they were hoping for, and the stage culminated in the expected bunch sprint.

item.title: Nigel Farage meeting a 'shadowy foreign donor'? It can only be another establishment stitch-up | Marina Hyde
item.author: Marina Hyde
item.content:encoded: The only thing more dodgy than Reform’s financial dealings is the egregious lunchtime combination of oysters, Guinness and champagneHow many sarcastic air quotes is too many for quoting Nigel Farage’s suggestion that Reform have been ““““““““hoaxed”””””””” by some undercover investigators into appearing to seek to get round electoral law to bag a £500k donation from a foreigner, as well as commissioning off-the-books polling and failing to identify it to newspapers? I don’t feel eight was too many. I could run to nine. Amazing, really, that it’s been as long as a few weeks since Farage had a crash-out and forced a byelection. All any of us wants is for Nigel to once again resign after a staged shitfit and ask a few thousand members of the public to judge him.For whatever reason, though, the law of our country does not amount to an “ONLY THE PEOPLE OF CLACTON CAN JUDGE ME” tattoo, and so it is that as Reform’s conference gets under way today, the party has been reported to the police for allegedly using foreign money to fund its activities. It’s all based on a covert sting carried out by Verbatim – an investigative group founded by journalists from the non-profit Centre for Climate Reporting – and broadcast last night on Channel 4 News.Marina Hyde is a Guardian columnistDo you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? item.title: Rocket Report: Engines installed for Artemis III; Long March 6C breakup in LEO
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: Welcome to Edition 9.09 of the Rocket Report! This edition includes an update from Blue Origin on the groundbreaking of a new Payload Processing Facility in Florida. It has been about a month since the company offered any meaningful news on its heavy-lift New Glenn rocket, which remains grounded after an on-pad explosion at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in May. The official line from Blue Origin is that the company is targeting a return to flight with New Glenn by the end of the year, but there's good reason for skepticism.As always, we welcome reader submissions. If you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets, as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.Isar Aerospace is ready to try again. Isar Aerospace is about to make the next attempt to launch the Spectrum rocket into orbit, with a weeklong launch window set to open Friday at Andøya Spaceport in Norway, the Norwegian Broadcasting Corporation (NRK) reports. The German launch company aims to deliver several small CubeSats to orbit with the two-stage Spectrum rocket. A test flight of the privately funded launcher failed shortly after liftoff last year, and Isar has attempted to launch the second Spectrum rocket several times since January, only to be thwarted by technical problems and the unavailability of the launch range in northern Norway.

item.title: Decathlon CMA CGM lose key climber as Gregor Mühlberger crashes out of ninth overall on stage 13 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Felix Gall is down a key climbing lieutenant at the Vuelta a España after his Decathlon CMA CGM teammate Gregor Mühlberger crashed out of the race in the early kilometres of stage 13.The 32-year-old Austrian has been in some of the best form of his career in Spain, emerging as one of the most impressive climbers in the race so far.Mühlberger has been part of a strong Decathlon CMA CGM lineup at the Vuelta, supporting Gall's GC aspirations and assisting the German to a current third place overall, 2:06 behind current leader Enric Mas (Movistar).He's been Gall's top climbing domestique so far, and was on course for a career-best Grand Tour finish of his own, lying ninth overall in the standings after Thursday's mountain stage to Calar Alto.Standout rides from Mühlberger include 10th-place finishes in Andorra and Calar Alto, plus 12th on the Alto de Aitana, all while working at the front of the race on behalf of Gall.However, Gall will have to do without the Tour of Austria winner for the final week of the race after Mühlberger was caught in a crash in the first 30km of the 193km stage 13 to Loja.Mühlberger was able to resume racing after falling, but he was announced as a DNF moments later. His loss is a major blow for Decathlon CMA CGM and Gall, and he becomes the 26th rider to leave the race.It remains to be seen what injuries Mühlberger sustained in the crash.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Lidl-Trek Future rider forced to swerve to avoid oncoming driver in concerning time trial incident
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Three weeks after Finlay Tarling's death after being struck by a driver at the Volta a Portugal, a rider was once again put at risk at the opening stage of the 2.2-ranked German race, the Sauerlandrundfahrt.In TV footage shared on social media, Lidl-Trek Future rider Louis Leidert could be seen swerving to avoid an oncoming driver while he raced the 13.7km opening time trial in Brilon. The driver managed to slow and mount the kerb to avoid Leidert.Moments later, Leidert was forced to brake and take evasive action once more as a driver, this time heading in the same direction, turned off the road just ahead of him.21-year-old German racer Leidert thankfully managed to avoid any collisions during his ride and raced to sixth place in the time trial, 33 seconds down on stage winner Ben Zwiehoff (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe Rookies).Sauerlandrundfahrt organisers released a statement on Friday morning, saying that they are taking the incidents seriously and have tightened security measures for the remaining three stages of the race.The statement does not explain how the two drivers accessed the barriered race course on stage 1."During the first stage of the Sauerlandrundfahrt, an incident occurred in which two vehicles entered the official time trial course despite the barriers. Fortunately, there was no accident, although one rider was forced to swerve out of the way," the statement read."We are very glad that nothing more serious happened in this instance. At the same time, we are taking the incident very seriously and are investigating it thoroughly. It goes without saying that it is not in our interest for such a situation to arise – the safety of all riders is our top priority."For the upcoming stages 2, 3 and 4, we have therefore, in collaboration with the police, the public order office, our stewards and the volunteers, significantly tightened security measures once again."We will do everything in our power to ensure that such an incident does not happen again."The incident isn't the first to occur since Tarling's death when he was hit by an oncoming driver on stage 8 of the Volta a Portugal.Less than a week later, at the Tour of Britain Women, O'Shea Chilli Bikes racer Maeve Plouffe took to social media to detail her experience during stage 1 of the race.Plouffe narrowly avoided being hit, she said: "On a side note, while the race convoy was still in sight and I was less than two minutes down, there were cars from the general public coming at me from all directions, including one that nearly hit me on a roundabout."Later on, the moto escort was wonderful and I felt much safer. But considering the recent devastating events in our cycling community, it's scary to see situations like this, when we know that this can have horrific consequences, especially so soon after suffering such a tragedy."Like Leidert, Plouffe was lucky to avoid being hit, though she didn't make it to the end of the stage after chasing alone at the back of the race for over half an hour.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'I want to write my own story' – Who is Jakob Omrzel? Meet the next Slovenian star who's not interested in comparisons to Pogačar and Roglič
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Any Slovenian prospect who emerges as a top climber will naturally be compared to the two modern greats still operating in the peloton, five-time Grand Tour winner Primož Roglič and five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogačar, but for Jakob Omrzel, who announced himself with a victory at the Vuelta a España on Thursday, he's more interested in forging his own path. In reality, anyone following the under-23 ranks would have known Omrzel's name already, a winner of Paris-Roubaix juniors and the Giro d'Italia Next Gen just last season, but a win at the Vuelta, only his second pro victory after claiming the elite Slovenian road race title in 2025, propels him into new ground. Not only this, but his success from the breakaway has jumped him right up into the top six overall at the Vuelta a España, and with more high mountains to come, he could well hold on for a top GC finish at the first attempt. Already mixing it with the seniors last year at 19, Omrzel has gone from strength to strength in 2026 as a 20-year-old, and he looks set to be a name to follow closely in the coming years, alongside the likes of Paul Seixas and Lorenzo Finn. sat down with him back in the off-season ahead of the Grand Canaria 365 Gran Fondo last year to find out more about how he came to be a top climbing prospect, and why it's important that he forges his own story, instead of one already written by Pogačar – who he trained with that week – and Roglič.A lot can happen in 10 months though, with his confidence, assuredness, and maturity as a rider shining through on stage 12 of the Vuelta, and back when we spoke, he wasn't even thinking about Grand Tours, let alone winning a stage of one. But the path to this recent success was clear even then, as a talent rapidly on the rise, and from one of the nations we've come to see dominate modern cycling.Cyclingnews: How did you get into cycling in Slovenia when you were younger? Where did that start for you?It started in fifth grade for me because my brother was cycling at the time, and for me I was always looking at my brother and wanting to do things that he was doing at the time. So yeah, sure, he dragged me into cycling, and the story continues from that on. CN: And was that only on the road straight away, or did you try other disciplines like mountain biking? No, no, no, road. It was always road because in Slovenia it's more like road. I mean, it was developed more for road, but now OK, MTB is also getting bigger. But still, it was for sure always the love for road for me.CN: You're one of the rising young stars of the peloton and would have grown up watching and Tadej Pogačar; were these guys your icons already growing up? Yeah, of course. I mean, it's really nice because not long ago, like three, four years, I was just like looking at them and, really, these guys are incredible, and now I'm finding myself in this position that I can be with them, train with them and race with them; it's just incredible. For sure, the dream's coming true. CN: With Tadej, you've spent some time training and riding with him. What's that been like for you? Maybe strange, but also exciting? Exactly this. It's really strange because you're with the best guy in the world that you always watch on TV. But in the end, OK, now here we are, and for sure we also need to be competitive – maybe not on that level. It's just incredible to be with these guys and to learn from them.CN: How would you describe yourself as a rider? I would say I'm more of an endurance guy. If the race is longer, for me, it's better. Also, on the bike, sometimes I can get nervous, but I think this is totally normal because of adrenaline and everything. I would say otherwise I'm a pretty calm guy, but yeah, sometimes it's stressful. CN: I think you've made a point of saying you're not trying to be the next Tadej or the next Primož; you want to be yourself. Why was that important for you as a GC prospect to just be you? Because you get all this pressure from the media or from other people who are saying, 'Oh, you're a new Pogačar, you're a new Roglič,' and for me, I mean, I don't like this because I am what I am, and I don't know what I'm going to do.I'm still young. I'm 19 [now 20]. Everything can change, but it's all OK if you are going in the right direction and if you have the people around you who are supporting you and are just leading you in the right way. I think that I want to write my own story. So we'll see how Jakob's story will end. But for sure, I just want to be myself. I will build this up for myself, and that's it. CN: How did you know you were ready for the WorldTour after just one year on Bahrain Victorious' development team? When I started at U23 level, I was always feeling confident, and basically, in my first year, I achieved a lot, and together with the team, we thought 'OK, it's now time to go up a level and try there'. Also, already [in 2025] I was introduced to it, and you have all the benefits of the highest level. cyclist. I think this was just the right step forward, but sure, we'll see. CN: How have you found the transition into the WorldTour squad?The change is very big. You can feel it because there are a lot more people that are involved in this than in devo; it's just a different level. I wouldn't say different mentality because we're still the same guys, but everything is more serious. You need to be 100% in everything, but in devo, I was nowhere near it. Now everything is a bit more specific, and we're doing things that are just different, but for me, this is something incredible, something to learn each day. CN: There's a big Slovenian influence on this team, but also throughout the peloton now. What's the best advice you've had from guys like or even Tadej Pogačar on a different team? For sure, that I'm young, and I still need to be calm and just work, work, and work my way up. Sometimes be quieter and just listen to other people and learn, learn, learn, and eventually, for sure, if you learn enough, you'll get the result you want. Just this: be smart. CN: Do you feel that there is pressure for you to win immediately in the WorldTour as one of these top talents, or has the team allowed room for you to be patient?I can feel that in my team there was no pressure because it was not planned that I would go in the WorldTour [this year]. It was just a natural process that I went up; no one was really pushing me. I put pressure on myself for results because I could see that I have the potential to win, and that's it. But also now for WorldTour, it's nothing like 'you need to win'. We will develop, and we'll try as much as we can, but without harming my body and just go with the flow. CN: There's loads to pick from, but what's the one race you dream of winning? For sure, the Tour de France; that is the dream.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: ‘They disturb the game’: how betting fans are taking over tennis courts
item.author: Tumaini Carayol at Flushing Meadows
item.content:encoded: Jeering and heckling are increasingly commonplace, even at grand slams, as spectators try to influence matchesMidway through the first week of the US Open a couple of years ago, Jiri Lehecka’s attempts to find his form were disrupted by incessant taunting from a spectator close by. “There was a guy who sat just behind my bench on a smaller court, court four, and he was talking to me basically for the first three sets, like non-stop,” Lehecka says. “He was talking to me like: ‘You can’t do it. You are tired. He’s better than you are.’”Lehecka maintained his composure and closed out the match, but even as he focused on navigating the intense stress of competition, he believed he understood this spectator’s motivations. The spectator, he thinks, was not there just to cheer for his favourite player: he was a bettor who had put money on Lehecka to lose. He had entered court four solely to influence the outcome of the match.Continue reading...

item.title: Gasly loses Monaco GP podium as penalties reinstated following McLaren and Red Bull appeal
Nearly impossible? How Fairphone built the ethical, repairable Fairphone Gen 6+
item.author: Ryan Whitwam
item.content:encoded: Smartphone longevity didn't used to matter. In the past, before you could wear out or break a phone, there was always some shiny new thing to buy. Today, we expect our smartphones to go the distance, but they've also become less repairable and, in many cases, more fragile. Fairphone, a Dutch smartphone maker that has just entered the US market, thinks about phones differently.The new $650 Fairphone Gen 6+ is designed both for longevity and easy repairability. There are trade-offs to this approach if you're used to the standard glass and aluminum sandwiches filled with glue, gaskets, and teeny-tiny screws. But the drawbacks could be worth it for the right buyer. Fairphone CTO Chandler Hatton told Ars that Fairphone's goal is to provide a compelling mobile experience while also enabling the user to "fully own" their device. At the end of the day, this is what a lot of people say they want in a smartphone.Take it apart, put it back togetherThese days, Google, Samsung, and Apple support phones with software updates for the better part of a decade, but will the hardware last that long? And what happens when it needs a repair? You may be out of luck or out a lot of money, but Fairphone prioritizes the self-repair experience.

item.title: As it happened: victory goes to the breakaway on tactical stage 13 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hello and welcome to stage 13 of the Vuelta a España!September 4, 2026 – 6:27 AMYou join us as the peloton is in Almuñécar, a first venture into the province of the Granada where this race will return to for its end just over a week from now. They're making their way through the (long) neutralised section, ahead of what we're anticipating to be a huge battle to get up the road on what looks like a nailed-on day for the breakaway. September 4, 2026 – 6:32 AMThere are three official climbs to be taken on, and they're front-loaded, making an inviting springboard for any strong climbers who want to get into the break. And potentially any GC threats wanting to leap up the rankings? It will likely be very hard to control at the start of the day, and race leader Enric Mas' Movistar team will need to be on their toes. September 4, 2026 – 6:36 AMThe peloton is down another rider, as NSN’s Alexey Lutsenko failed to make the start today. He had looked in his best form for a long time, too, finishing fourth yesterday atop Calar Alto, and getting into many breakaways throughout the race. Unfortunately, he fell ill last night.September 4, 2026 – 6:40 AMSeptember 4, 2026 – 6:48 AMThe first 10 or 15km of this stage are flat, and so pose a chance for non-climbers to get into the break before the road ramps upwards. Four such riders are on the attack, and lead by 25 seconds - Domen Novak, Enzo Paleni, Asbjørn Hellemose and Fabio Van den BosscheSeptember 4, 2026 – 6:55 AMThe lead of the four riders has grown some more to 40 seconds. No pursuers are between them and the peloton for now, but that's sure to change once the climb starts, especially while the gap between them remains so bridgeable. September 4, 2026 – 7:03 AMThe four leaders are about to start the climb with a lead on the peloton of 55 seconds, while a lone pursuer (Urko Berrade, who was second yesterday) is ten second ahead of the peloton.This is the hardest climb of the day, the only one rated category one, and the longest, lasting 14.1km at 5.1%. Brace yourselves - this is where attacks from the peloton will ignite!September 4, 2026 – 7:11 AMNo pursuing group has formed yet as they take on the lower slopes of the climb. The gap to the leaders has come down, to 30 seconds.September 4, 2026 – 7:19 AMThe break is caught, as the pace in the peloton is increased. Astana's Fortunato has replaced them at the front of the road, but there is surely much more attacking to come as they approach the summit of the climb.September 4, 2026 – 7:25 AMGall's key climbing domestique Gregor Mühlberger has gone down in a crash on the climb. That's potentially worrying news for Gall, as the Austrian has been crucial to him in the climbs of this Vuelta, but he's back on his bike and riding so has hopefully not been affected. September 4, 2026 – 7:31 AMA big group of about 30 riders have gone clear, before the summit. As well as Fortunato, many other eye-catching names are in it - King of the Mountains Buitrago, stage winner Leknessund, and the deadly Visma duo of Van Aert and Brennan.September 4, 2026 – 7:37 AMThe group's not being allowed to go clear just yet, the peloton keeping them at 20 seconds.There are lots of strong climbers in it, and a few who could stand to break into the top ten - in fact, all of the riders currently ranked between 11th - 14th are in it (Berthet, Cristián Rodríguez, Bisiaux and Riccitello).September 4, 2026 – 7:42 AMAs was the case yesterday, once again Van Aert and Buitrago sprinted for the KOM points, taking first and second respectively, followed by Fortunato, De la Cruz and Rodriguez. Here's what the updated rankings look like:September 4, 2026 – 7:47 AMThe action is still very much on, and multiple other riders have bridged from the peloton to join this lead group - among them Skjelmose, who is still up in seventh at 7:42, and a threat on GC. With more than 40 riders up the road, Movistar have to keep this under control, and for now the peloton remains within 40 seconds of them.September 4, 2026 – 7:52 AMBad news for Decathlon CMA CGM - Gregor Mühlberger has left the race following his crash earlier. Not only was he himself ninth on GC, he was performing sterling work for leader Felix Gall. Gall might not yet have managed to successfully utilise his compatriot and teammate to take the red jersey, but it will become a lot harder now without him.September 4, 2026 – 7:59 AMVisma-Lease a Bike are well-placed in this group, with Armirail also present to do the pulling along with leaders Van Aert and Brennan. They're not the best-represented team here, though - Uno-X have four, including previous stage winner Leknessund and runner-up Cort.September 4, 2026 – 8:04 AMWidar and Martin were also part of the group of riders who bridged up to this lead group, which means every rider between 11th - 16th on GC is in it.They’re looking to make a leap into the top a la Jakob Omrzel, who is now up to 6th overall after so brilliantly winning yesterday’s stage. The Slovenian caught the attention of the cycling world with that ride, but remains little-known - learn more about the latest prodigious Slovenian talent here.September 4, 2026 – 8:13 AMThe break is splitting into groups on the rolling terrain they’re taking on ahead of the day’s second (official) climb. Rodriguez, Kron and Elosegui (pictured) stole a march on the others to go clear, and a chase group of Brennan, Leknessund, Miguel, Molard and Laurance have formed behind them.The gap are still close between all these splits, with the larger chasing breakaway group just 20seconds behind the leaders, but the peloton is now two minutes adrift. September 4, 2026 – 8:18 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 4, 2026 – 8:22 AMThe various splits in the breakaway group came back together again, and now three new riders have attacked out of it to go clear - Brennan, Leknessund and Vermaerke. This break is simply too big to function as a whole, and these attacks will consequently keep coming. September 4, 2026 – 8:30 AMThe breakaway is in bits. Brennan, Leknessund and Vermaerke have been joined by Martin, Laurance and Albanese, while more riders are chasing up to them in small groups. The situation might become more stable once they start climbing in a few kilometres, up the 5.8km, 4.9% Alto del Legionario. September 4, 2026 – 8:38 AMThe 6 leaders are now 9, with Rodríguez, Berthet and Kron joining them. They're also building more of an advantage now they've started the climb, and are over 40 seconds ahead of the rest of the break. September 4, 2026 – 8:44 AMInterestingly, it's EF Education-EasyPost who are leading the peloton, rather than Mas' Movistar. They could be riding out of fear of the threat posed to Carapaz's fourth-place; but could they also be plotting something to launch him up the road? The Ecuadorian is famous for his aggression, so you can never count it out.September 4, 2026 – 8:47 AMBisiaux and Craps have bridged up to the leading group, brining its number up to 11. There's now a gap between them and the chase group of 30 seconds - things could be at breaking point, and if the chasers don't work together, their hopes of winning the stage might disappear already. September 4, 2026 – 8:56 AMAnother abandon for UAE, who's Pavel Sivakov joins Pogačar, Torres and Vine in leaving the race. The team hasn't managed to bounce back in quite the way as was anticipated following their leader's withdrawal, although they have Vermaerke up the road in the lead group. Sivakov is the fourth abandon of the day, following Mühlberger, Busatto and Sentjens.September 4, 2026 – 9:00 AMBoth Van Aert and Buitrago missed the split, and therefore weren't around to compete for the KOM points. Instead, they went to Albanese, Martin and Kron.The riders are now descending the climb, the leading nine one having grown their lead to the chasers to one minute, and to the peloton to four minutes. September 4, 2026 – 9:03 AMThe pace remains high and the lead group want to put the chasers out of sight. But Axel Laurance presses on a bit too hard going round a corner, and hits the deck. He's up and riding, but is now caught in no-man's land behind the eight leaders, and the large group of chasers. September 4, 2026 – 9:10 AMEnric Mas in the peloton in red, who, despite the size of the breakaway group, is having a fairly straightforward day, especially as his Movistar team is getting help from EF leading the bunch in response to Skjelmose's presence in it. The Spaniard is enjoying the kind of form he has rarely, if ever, had throughout his career, and wants to make the most of it to win a first ever Grand Tour title.September 4, 2026 – 9:15 AMThis is looking good for the ten leaders. The chase group (now lacking De La Cruz, who is back in the peloton after becoming the latest rider to crash) is now 1:30 adrift, and not working well enough together to bridge the gap. September 4, 2026 – 9:20 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 4, 2026 – 9:29 AM It's not over yet, but if the advantage of the lead group (pictured) can grow much beyond its current time of 1:30, they will be difficult to catch. And the peloton are currently chasing to control Skjelmose, who is in the chasing group - if that's neutralised you imagine they will be happy to let the break contest the stage. September 4, 2026 – 9:38 AMToday’s finale isn’t hard enough for Primož Roglič to attack, but he will need to go on the offensive at some point if he’s to take the red jersey from Enric Mas, now that the deficit has grown. Overall victory remains the clear goal, and Roglič can’t just rely on the third week time trial to make up the time.September 4, 2026 – 9:48 AMThe race is in a holding pattern, as the leading ten continue to focus on maintaining their lead over the chasers, which is at 1:30, and the peloton, which is 4:30. At some point, they will have to switch to start thinking about how to beat each other the win to win the stage, especially considering the fastest finisher of the race, Matthew Brennan, is in it. The others will likely start to attack him come the next, and final, climb, coming up in about 20km.September 4, 2026 – 9:55 AMStill the leaders work well together, as the chasers remain 1:30 adrift. The latter are on a difficult situation, as by pacing they're also giving Brennan's teammate Van Aert a free ride. But from Visma's perspective, Brennan is in a vulnerable position in the lead group as everyone will be aware of the need to attack him. September 4, 2026 – 10:02 AMAnother factor to consider is how hot it is out there. Some riders reported suffering in the conditions yesterday, and temperatures are again nearing 40 degrees.September 4, 2026 – 10:09 AMMovistar continue to do most of the work in the peloton, with a little help from EF, but they're been losing ground on the front groups. They're now 4:45 behind the leaders and 3:45 ahead of the Skjelmose group, which is enough to see the Dane leap to fifth on the virtual GC.September 4, 2026 – 10:13 AMBrennan takes the 20 points on offer at the intermediate sprint, partly to defend his teammate's Van Aert's lead partly to solidify his own place in second in the classification. Here's what it looks like now:September 4, 2026 – 10:18 AMWe've entered a crucial part of the stage now, as the riders start climbing the final hill of the day, the category two Puerto de Granada. Its average of 5.6% for 7.4km is hard enough to cause selections in the front group, especially as everyone there is fully aware of the need to drop Brennan.September 4, 2026 – 10:21 AMThis is an interesting development. The chase group have slashed the advantage to the leaders, to just 30 seconds - and it's down to work done by Visma's Armirail. The team have made the call that they don't believe Brennan can win from the front group, and are instead trying to bring back the chase group to get Van Aert back into contention. It's a big call, especially as Brennan looks comfortable so far on the climb and hasn't come under any attacks. A lot of pressure would be on Van Aert to deliver the win for them.September 4, 2026 – 10:27 AMAttack from Vermaerke! As Armirail brings the chase group to within 15 seconds of the leaders, the UAE riders responds. He's caught, but is countered by Leknessund. Hostilities have ignited. September 4, 2026 – 10:30 AMIt's all kicking off now, as Van Aert takes matters into his own hands. He's taken off the front, and is picking off riders who are being dropped from the first group, with a handful of riders just about managing to cling on to his wheel.Up ahead, Leknessund has been caught by several riders, including Brennan. September 4, 2026 – 10:35 AMVermaerke attacks out of the lead group at the summit, and leads a group of four over the summit. But behind them both chase groups are mere seconds behind, and have rejoined on the descent.So we now have a group of almost 20 together, including both Brennan and Van Aert, plus Buitrago, Skjelmose, Widar, Rodríguez and Berthet. Visma are looking good, but the stage win is still wide open, with 35km still to ride. September 4, 2026 – 10:40 AMNow in the front group, Van Aert is on a mission. He's tried an attack, and though the rest of the group have just about managed to bridge up to him, he looks fresh. Visma now have the luxury of having both cards of Van Aert and Brennan to play - but they're lacking a domestique, as Armirail was used up in the earlier chase. September 4, 2026 – 10:44 AMVan Aert and Brennan are now attacking in tandem, and the others are struggling to follow. The group has been reduced to about ten riders, though Skjelmose is still present, and is now up to fourth on the virtual GC.September 4, 2026 – 10:51 AMVan Aert's latest attack saw him go clear with Vermaerke and Paret-Peintre. Neither of them offered a turn, and they've been brought back, but more attacks are surely on the way in this breathless finale. September 4, 2026 – 10:54 AMThere are only seven riders left with Van Aert and Brennan - Vermaerke, Fisher-Black, Bisiaux, Paret-Peintre, Widar, Albanese and Dalby. Vermaerke appears to be one of the strongest, and just tried his own attack, but Van Aert managed to mark it. September 4, 2026 – 10:59 AMThings have calmed down a little in the lead group of nine, with no attacks in the last few kilometres. The other riders present will be very aware of the threat posed by the two Visma riders, both of whom none of them will want to have to sprint against. Surely they will have to attack if they want to win the stage. September 4, 2026 – 11:02 AMSkjelmose hasn't made the split into this front group, and is among the chasers who are now 1:11. In turn, they're 3:10 ahead of the peloton, which means as things stand he'll move up to fifth on the virtual GC - which isn't quite as big a leap as he poised to make earlier. September 4, 2026 – 11:06 AMAfter a pause without attacks, Bisiaux attempts a move, and looks very strong. It took a big effort from Brennan to bring him back, while Fisher-Black had to swing off.After the catch was made, Vermaerke tried again, and this time Van Aert covers it. This is still hectic, but Visma are controlling things for now. September 4, 2026 – 11:10 AMAfter moved from Bisiaux and Dalby, Van Aert launches a move about 4km from the finish - and it's a big one! Only Paret-Peintre can follow, and there's a gap growing to the rest.September 4, 2026 – 11:12 AMVan Aert and Paret-Peintre are away and out of sight from the others! Paret-Peintre is offering a few turns, but Van Aert appears happy to do the lion's share, knowing he will surely beat him in a two-up sprint. September 4, 2026 – 11:15 AMParet-Peintre gave it a good go, and was even side-by-side with Van Aert for some of the sprint, but it's the Belgian who takes the win, his first of this year's Vuelta.Brennan then completes a perfect day for Visma-Lease a Bike by winning the sprint in the group behind for third. September 4, 2026 – 11:19 AMSeptember 4, 2026 – 11:25 AMAfter a big effort from Decathlon, the peloton arrived at the line three minutes after Van Aert, and, more pertinently, 2:10 behind the Skjelmose group.That means that, despite all his efforts, Skjelmose doesn't actually move up the GC rankings, but remains seventh; albeit now to within 33 seconds of him on GC, Omrzel.September 4, 2026 – 11:28 AMSeptember 4, 2026 – 11:34 AMElsewhere, the third stage of the Tour of Britain concluded earlier today. You can read all about what happened here.September 4, 2026 – 11:43 AMHere's Van Aert on the podium as stage winner. Though he's had a strong Vuelta, as evidenced by his big lead in the points classification and his surprise second place ranking in the King of the Mountains, but the much-wanted stage win had been elusive until now. He's taken seven wins since his golden day at Paris-Roubaix, but this is the biggest one so far. September 4, 2026 – 11:49 AMThanks for joining us today! Away from all the stage-hunting drama, Enric Mas successfully defended the red jersey for another day, the jersey he still hopes to wear when the riders return to Granada at the end of net week.Tomorrow will be a big test of whether or not he will do so, as the stage finishes with yet another big summit finish, the Sierra de La Panders. With the GC race still so open, many fireworks are again promised, so be sure to return to us for all of the action.

item.title: Worker strikes possible in Montreal during Road World Championships
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: There is a threat of strikes during the UCI Road World Championships in Montreal, Canada, later this month, after a workers' union in Quebec proposed seven days of industrial action from September 22-28.As reported by , the Syndicat des cols bleus regroupés de Montréal (SCFP 301), which represents blue-collar workers – those who work outside of offices, for example, construction and municipal workers – announced on Wednesday that they had filed notice to strike from 6am to 6pm for seven days later this month, pending negotiations.The union has 143,000 members in the province of Quebec, including some 70% of municipal employees, and members in transportation, education, and the fire service, among other sectors.At present, the strike is not confirmed, and the union is still in negotiations with the city of Montreal, primarily surrounding wage increases and the renewal of their collective agreement."We have just completed an intense round of negotiations, and the employer side does not seem to have a clear mandate regarding monetary terms. The City is still offering wage increases below inflation. Montreal’s blue-collar workers provide an essential service and deserve at least some seriousness at the bargaining table,” union president Nicolas De Ciccio said.According to , the union has clarified that 'essential services' would be maintained during any strike, but industrial action would surely be disruptive to the week-long event, which is expected to attract thousands of spectators, and would require city support for road closures and emergency services. also notes that the union has previously criticised the city of Montreal for using private companies to resurface roads ahead of the Road World Championships. The union also staged a 72-hour strike earlier this year.Negotiations are still ongoing, with a possibility that strike action can be avoided. De Ciccio said "there's no way we're going to agree to sign a collective agreement that would lead to the impoverishment of our members. We're not asking for the moon." contacted the organisers of the Montréal World Championships, who declined to comment.With just over three weeks until the proposed strike start, there is still time for strike action to be avoided, or for mitigation plans to be put in place. item.title: It’s time for Mark Zuckerberg to resign from Meta | Joan Donovan
item.author: Joan Donovan
item.content:encoded: The CEO is the throughline in a history of billion-dollar blunders that have caused real harm, culminating in last week’s settlementLast week, Meta, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, agreed to a settlement of up to $18bn after dozens of US states accused it of harming children with addictive products. The settlement’s regulatory implications for social media will affect every user, far beyond teens.But if Meta is truly interested in prioritizing the safety of users, the board should request the resignation of Mark Zuckerberg and restructure to put safety above profit.Continue reading...

item.title: Private equity faces existential crisis in US as unsold companies pile up
item.author: Heather Timmons
item.content:encoded: Private equity firms and the companies they own employ over 13 million, from startups to rural hospitals and large retailers, but experts’ concerns of collapse are growingRetail stalwarts Saks and Eddie Bauer filed for bankruptcy. Kmart and JoAnn Fabrics are gone for good, a trail of layoffs and disappointed customers in their wake. Hospital giant Steward Health Care collapsed, costing thousands of jobs and leaving several communities without a local hospital.These once-trusted US companies have one thing in common: they were owned by private equity investors, who load companies with debt when they buy them and squeeze out profits as they restructure.Continue reading...

item.title: 20-year-old Unbound Gravel 100 winner Kylee Hanel to get a taste of the WorldTour with Visma-Lease a Bike stagiaire contract
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Hanel has experience racing in Europe, having raced several Belgian kermesses last year. This year, she won the youth classification at the Tour of Gila Women, closing out the week with a win on the final stage in Pinos Altos. She's also the US under-23 time trial champion and leader of the gravel Life Time under-23 competition.Hanel, who hails from Oregon, will join Visma-Lease a Bike for this weekend's races, the Tout commence en Finistère and the Pointe du Raz."We are always looking for talented riders, and not only within the traditional road cycling world. Kylee caught our attention through her impressive performances," said Visma-Lease a Bike manager Rutger Tijssen."She has shown that she has a lot of potential, and we are curious to see how she can translate those qualities to the road. We see this as a great opportunity for her to gain experience with our team and for us to get to know her better as a rider."Hanel has been racing with the US club team Aegis x Leaders of Enchantment as the youngest rider in the team, which also includes Lauren Stephens, winner of the Redlands Bicycle Classic and Tour of the Gila Women."I have learned so much from her. I've not only learned positioning, bike handling skills, and teamwork from her, but the most important thing I learned from her is humility," she said."She knows it's a blessing to be racing and is appreciative of the fact that she gets to go out and race. She doesn't look at the world like it owes her something, which I admire a lot about her."It remains to be seen how Hanel will fare in her time with Visma-Lease a Bike, and whether the move will be made permanent beyond this stagiaireship. Later this month, she'll represent the USA at the Road World Championships in Canada, taking part in the under-23 time trial and road race for the first time.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Thieves target mail order sales as Pokémon card prices soar
item.author: Daniella Lucas
item.content:encoded: As one card recently sold for £12m, opportunistic thefts have surged – envelopes are being opened en route, costing small businesses thousandsPokémon’s success over the last 30 years has seen it grow from a much-loved Game Boy classic, to a world-dominating brand with TV shows, spin-off games, toys and even a theme park. The trading card game is a huge part of that, with more than 85bn cards printed over its lifetime, and the appetite for them shows no signs of slowing down. Packs get snapped up after release so quickly it’s now almost impossible to find them in shops, and a booming resale market is driving the hobby into murky waters.One card recently sold for an eye-watering £12m, and an increasing number of people have gotten into the collecting business on the hunt for huge profits, leading to a rise in thefts targeting card shops. More recently though, some small businesses have reported that their sales have been hit by thieves targeting envelopes within Royal Mail, leading to thousands in lost revenue.Continue reading...

item.title: More management exits at UAE Team L'IMAD as Cherie Pridham leaves for rival team
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: The management shake-up at UAE Team L'IMAD is set to continue with Head of Sports Cherie Pridham leaving the squad for pastures new, alongside sports director Dave Povall, following the departure of their team principal and other staff.Pridham and Povall will work for Human Powered Health in 2027, the American team announced on Thursday evening. The squad is going through their own building process with several high-profile rider signings for next year.In experienced sports director Pridham, who has worked across top-tier men's and women's teams for decades, the team is gaining serious expertise in the team car, joining head DS Magnus Bäckstedt.But whilst it's a seemingly positive move for Human Powered Health, it's a more concerning departure for UAE Team L'Imad, who have already seen significant changes to their senior leadership structure this season.Team principal Yana Seel left the team earlier in the summer, ending her contract early and citing "a divergence in our strategic visions for the team’s future development" as her reasoning in a statement given to Daniel Benson's Cycling Substack at the time.The team have been without a replacement principal since then, with an interim staff member stepping up to take on day-to-day running of the team whilst they looked for a full-time replacement. DS Michel Cornelisse is also confirmed to be leaving the team to join SD Worx-Protime, and there are uncertainties over the futures of DSs Lionel Marie and Paolo Slongo, who is Longo Borghini's personal coach. With Pridham, Povall and Cornelisse leaving, the squad is already losing a large portion of its performance team. According to , Pridham was in the running to step up into the role of principal, with team president Melissa Moncada saying: "I hope that she’s with the team. That’s not something that I have confirmation on. Cherie has been a valuable piece in our team. We’ve had many conversations with Cherie. [...] I hope that she continues."However, since the Tour de France Femmes – where Pridham led the team to finish on the podium, as well as fifth and seventh overall – the British director has clearly made her decision to depart for pastures new."For me, good leadership is about listening and understanding, while still being calm enough to make clear decisions and maintain high standards when the pressure is on," she said in a Human Powered Health press release.The reasons for the multiple departures at UAE Team L'Imad are not clear, and there have been more behind-the-scenes management shuffles over the past few years, but one possible source of tension is the future of Vuelta Femenina Paula Blasi, who is expected to break her contract to leave the squad early despite being one of their biggest talents.Moncada called the failure to secure Blasi's contract "a stupid mistake" in her interview with Daniel Benson, and narratives around Blasi's future and leadership – or lack thereof – at the Tour de France caused friction between the media and the team, who felt unfairly questioned over the situation. Answers to all of these questions are not yet clear, with no official word on Blasi's future, nor a new team principal in place at UAE just yet, but the continued departures do suggest that all is not yet settled at the team.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Injury forces WRC Chile co-driver change for Katsuta
SNY’s Ian Begley Reveals Two Knicks Free-Agent Targets for Final Roster Spots
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks still have work to do before opening their NBA championship defense, with 13 players on guaranteed contracts and a particular need for additional depth behind their established centers.On Thursday, SNY’s Ian Begley reported that veterans Drew Eubanks and John Konchar are among the free agents on New York’s radar as training camp approaches.“Per SNY sources, guard-forward John Konchar and forward-center Drew Eubanks are among the players on New York’s radar as we draw closer to training camp,” Begley reported. “Konchar, recently waived and stretched after a trade to Minnesota, is known as a strong rebounder/defender/offensive connector who can knock down perimeter shots over his seven-year NBA career. “Eubanks’ 2025-26 season in Sacramento was cut short in March following surgery to repair a UCL tear in his left thumb. The 6-foot-10 veteran would presumably be competing with a couple of other big men for the Knicks’ third center spot.“Eubanks would obviously address the more obvious positional need, as New York currently has Karl-Anthony Towns as its starting center and uber-veteran Andre Drummond as the lone backup, following the exits of Mitchell Robinson and Ariel Hukporti.The 29-year-old spent last season with the Sacramento Kings, averaging 5.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 0.6 blocks in 13.1 minutes per game, but injuries limited him to just 42 appearances.As expected, Begley suggested that Eubanks’ deal, if signed, would likely be non-guaranteed and that the veteran would face competition for the third-center position, à la Brogdon-Mathews-Shamet last summer.Konchar, meanwhile, would offer the Knicks a much-different option for one of their two final spots. The 30-year-old guard-forward became available after Minnesota waived him after trading for him last week.Konchar averaged 4.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals across 56 games with Memphis and the Jazz last season.Still, don’t trip. The Knicks have two standard roster openings, yes, but the Knicks are also expected to begin the season with only 14 players because of 1) their proximity to the second tax apron and 2) . Hooray!Anyway, New York has more than a month remaining before beginning its championship defense, with Begley reporting that its final roster decisions are still being evaluated and most likely down to the wire once training camp and preseason are completed, and the Knicks know everything they know about their prospective candidates.

item.title: 'Believe that this was the best achievable solution under the circumstances' – Organisers respond to criticism of women's elite start schedule at European Gravel Championships
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: The UEC Gravel European Championships start schedule packed the release of the elite and age group fields into thirty minutes on Sunday, with the elite men heading off to take on three laps of the course first, while the elite women's start came after the bulk of the men's age group categories had set off.The interval between the elite women and the 65-74 men in the race, which was also part of the UCI Gravel World Series, was just five minutes. The 60-64 group was also a further two minutes back, and the 55-59 riders also started within 10 minutes of the elite women. That gave the top women battling for a European title approximately 2km of clear air before they started to mingle with the men's age group categories ahead, leaving a number among the elite women's field describing what unfolded next as more of a 'slalom' or 'game of Pac-Man' than a gravel race."I completely agree that the current situation can still be improved and that the concerns raised are legitimate," said Erwin Vervecken, UCI Gran Fondo & Gravel World Series manager, in reply to an email sent by requesting comment on the situation."However, based on the feedback received from the elite women's survey and the practical limitations related to permits, road closures and available time frame, we currently believe that this was the best achievable solution under the circumstances.""That said, this remains a topic that we continue to evaluate. Experience has shown that after several successful editions, local authorities can sometimes become more receptive to longer road closures and larger gaps between start groups. Wherever opportunities arise to further improve race conditions and safety for all participants, we will certainly explore them."The survey Vervecken is referring to was one conducted at the end of last season, coming about after concerns were raised following Gravel One Fifty in the Netherlands, where the elite women started behind the elite men and ahead of the age group categories, leading to a situation that drew criticism after they were caught relatively early in the race by some of the nearest starting men's age group categories.The survey question, shared by the UCI series, asked: 'In an ideal world, women have a separate race starting long before or after the men, but in reality, few organisers get the authorisation to close down roads for a long period. Given this remark, how would you suggest to best apply the starting procedure to have a fair and safe women's race?"Of the alternatives offered, the one chosen most often among those who responded to the survey was "Women should start after all male age categories, with an interval as big as possible. It's better to pass slower men's age groups than being caught by faster men."This was written into the series start procedure for events with more than 1,500 riders, the regulations stating that "women’s elite start must take place after all male age‑group starts, also those doing a shorter distance" and specified that the gap before the elite women's start "must be the largest possible, considering traffic-management limits and overlap-prevention".The five minutes the elite women's field had as a gap at the European Championships, which had 1,800 riders, was the biggest of the starting margins between categories – they were mostly at three minutes – but it was also considerably less than at many key series events.At Gravel One Fifty this year, the elite women's field started after all the men's age groups doing the same distance, which ends at the 55-59 age bracket, with a 13-minute gap. For another of the bigger events in the series, SEVEN, the gap was 15 minutes, while at The Gralloch it was closer to an hour, and other events even have a separation of days, not minutes."The ideal situation for the elite women's race is, of course, one where the athletes can compete in their own race with as little influence as possible from other categories," said Vervecken."Whenever this is organizationally feasible, such as at the UCI Gravel World Championships or at events held on separate race days like Graean Cymru (Wales), this approach is indeed implemented. Other events organised within fully controlled and closed venues, such as The Gralloch (Scotland), also have the possibility to start the women's race significantly earlier or later than other categories, as there is no impact on traffic management."At the same time, one of the greatest challenges in organising UCI Gravel events is securing sufficient road closure time from local authorities. In that regard, the situation has progressed considerably over the last few years. Where start intervals of only one minute between categories were common in the past, we now increasingly see gaps of three to five minutes between different start groups."There have long been issues around mixed fields in gravel, where the increasing ranks of professional riders line up alongside amateur athletes and drafting or interference among categories is an issue of contention, with several solutions being proposed and implemented across the varying strands of the discipline."The success of gravel is due to the combination of elites and age group participants who all share the same road and course, and we want to maintain that concept for future years, but also expect some understanding from the top-level elites," said Vervecken. "The men's elite have overtaken lots of lapped riders in the last part of their race, but we never heard any criticism from them."The elite men, however, faced different circumstances. They set off first, so had a clear full 47km lap of the course before hitting the then more spread-out traffic through their second and third laps, while the elite women's field had just a couple of kilometres before tackling the groups ahead which, that early in the race, had not had as much time to spread out.Vervecken said further meetings were being arranged with riders from the elite women's field to discuss the issue.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews.
