item.title: 'I want to win more races no matter what they are' – Lennert Van Eetvelt switches Lotto for NSN in three-year deal
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Van Eetvelt joins after racing for Lotto-Intermarché for the past four seasons, having come up through Lotto's development ranks.During his time as a pro, Van Eetvelt's standout results have included wins at the 2024 UAE Tour and Tour of Guangxi. He also has a podium at the 2024 Donostia San Sebastián Klasikoa to his name, as well as top-10 results at the Volta Catalunya, Strade Bianche, and Il Lombardia."Lennert Van Eetvelt is a rider we have followed closely over the past years, and we’re very pleased to welcome him to the team," said NSN general manager Kjell Carlström."Lennert has already demonstrated his ability to win at WorldTour level, particularly in demanding stage races, and we believe he can continue to develop over the coming seasons with us."After a strong 2024 campaign, Van Eetvelt's progress has seemed to stall in the past two seasons. The 25-year-old hasn't won a race since Guangxi two years ago, left his Tour de France debut last year following a crash, and made little impact on this year's race after going into it with a rib injury.Results have been more positive recently, however, with Van Eetvelt racing to second overall at the Arctic Race of Norway. He's set to take on the GPs de Québec and Montréal and Il Lombardia before the year is out.“What stands out is not only his climbing ability, but also the way he races. He is willing to take opportunities when they present themselves and has shown that he can finish off races against strong competition," Carlström said."Whether it's targeting the GC in stage races, the Ardennes classics, or showing what he can do in the mountains in Grand Tours, we are excited to see what Lennert can do in NSN colours."Having raced on junior squads in Belgium before joining the Lotto setup, Van Eetvelt said he's now looking forward to working in an international team for the first time."I was looking for an international and professional environment to take the next step in my career. NSN felt like the perfect fit for that, so I'm really looking forward to joining the team and seeing what we can do together over the next three years."I want to win more races no matter what they are. I know what my capabilities are, and I want to build the strongest palmarès I can from them, so I hope to hit the ground running in 2027. I'm confident I have made the right choice, and together, we will win races."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: The plastic waste overtaking New York – and the people trying to curb it
item.author: Photo essay by Bryan Anselm, words by Dharna Noor
item.content:encoded: From New York to Quebec, photographer Bryan Anselm spent months capturing spaces overrun with plastic and the actions individuals and groups are taking to reduce wasteIn New York City, the plastic we discard has a way of remaining in plain sight. There are few alleys to hide residents’ refuse, and the clear recycling bags leave their contents on full display. In a city built on a dense grid, lightweight wrappers, bags and bottles spill from overflowing bins and skitter down sidewalks, collecting in gutters and corners before the wind carries them on.All that plastic is a layer of the urban landscape, as familiar as subway grates and fire escapes, revealing a messy and unflattering aspect of city life. “Garbage is not what we cast out, but the prime locus of meaning in our lives,” the character Nick Shay says in Don DeLillo’s Underworld.Continue reading...

item.title: Fem van Empel says she's 'happier than ever' amid cycling career break
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: Fem van Empel has stated that she is "happier than ever," eight months into her career break from cycling. She has kept a low profile away from the sport since then but offered a glimpse into the reset it has provided with a social media update on Thursday, to mark her 24th birthday. "Little me would be so proud,' Van Empel wrote alongside a photo of herself as a child."Grateful where I stand today: healthier and happier then ever!! Cheers to 24 years."There is no indication at this point if Van Empel has any plans to return to cycling, but the latest post would indicate that the bold career pause has been very beneficial. Van Empel's troubles first emerged early in 2025, when, after winning her third straight cyclo-cross world title, she rode just two Classics on the road before announcing a mid-season break as the "best step for my mental health and well-being". She returned to action in September and planned to race a full cyclo-cross season, but by mid-December she had taken the decision to take an indefinite break from the sport. "This is a well-considered decision that I feel good about. At the moment, both the motivation and the enjoyment I have had in cycling for years are missing," Van Empel said at the time."I wanted to be honest and fair about this with the team. For now, this is the best choice. It feels like the right time for a new chapter. I am very grateful for all the support I have received from the team, my family, and the fans, and I look forward to what the future brings."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Florian Lipowitz returns to racing seven weeks on from Tour de France-ending crash – here's what's left of his season
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Seven weeks on from his Tour de France-ending crash, Florian Lipowitz is making his racing return, the German racer heading to the late-season Italian Classics to end his 2026 season.Lipowitz, along with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe co-leader Remco Evenepoel, was in contention for the Tour podium when he crashed during the stage 16 time trial in Thonon-les-Bains. He suffered a broken collarbone in the fall, which meant he left the race from fifth overall.On Wednesday, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe announced that the 25-year-old would make his return to the peloton at the Giro della Toscana on September 9."More than anything, I'm looking forward to pinning on a race number again and racing. After seven weeks without competition, I can't know exactly where I stand," Lipowitz said."That's what we want to find out. For me, these first races aren't about results. I want to see how my body responds to the demands of racing, get back into the rhythm and then decide together with the team what is still possible this season."Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe noted the race is part of a performance assessment ahead of the final weeks of the season.He's tentatively penned in for several more races, but participation will depend on how Toscana goes. The race is "less about achieving a result and more about establishing where Florian stands ahead of the remaining weeks of the season," the team said.If all goes well, Lipowitz should race on to the Coppa Sabatini (September 10), the Memorial Marco Pantani (September 12), and the Trofeo Matteotti (September 13)."When returning from an injury, the goal is not to get back to your previous training load as quickly as possible. We have to build load tolerance and performance in parallel," said team director of coaching, John Wakefield."With Florian, we saw early on that we were making good progress and that we could at least consider the originally planned return to racing a realistic goal. But the key is to assess every step based on how he responds to the load – not based on a date in the calendar."Lipowitz still has almost a week of training before returning to the peloton, but he's already thinking of bigger goals further ahead."Of course, the World Championships are a race that appeals to me. But one thing is also clear: if my form isn't good enough, I don't want to take a spot away from another rider," he said."We have a lot of strong German riders who are well suited to the course in Montréal. I want to wait for these first races and take an honest look at where I stand. If the form is there, I'd really like to race the Worlds – but I'm not putting any pressure on myself about that right now."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: UK homeowners: has the hot weather damaged your property?
item.author: Guardian community team
item.content:encoded: Are you dealing with subsidence or other issues caused by the hot weather? During a dry spell, such as the successive heatwaves that affected some parts of the UK this year, houses built on clay-rich soil suffer as moisture is sucked away by trees and bushes. This causes the clay to shrink and foundations to drop, causing structural problems.We would like to speak to homeowners who are dealing with damage to their homes which is likely to have been caused by this year’s extremely hot, dry weather.Continue reading...

They're about a minute behind the break.September 3, 2026 – 8:26 AMDíaz and Hamilton have joined the break. Sivakov hasn't made it. Should be 30 riders in the lead now.September 3, 2026 – 8:27 AMCorrection, Sivakov has made it, so 31 in the lead. Tracker is showing him as behind but we can see he is in the break.September 3, 2026 – 8:30 AMVan Aert wins maximum points again. He really is keen to go after this jersey, but he's only made up 2 points in his 11-point deficit to Buitrago.September 3, 2026 – 8:32 AMHere's a look at Wout van Aert in the break.Who do you think will win today? Break or peloton? Let me know in the comments.September 3, 2026 – 8:33 AMImages of Onley's crash, in case you missed it.September 3, 2026 – 8:35 AMSivakov confusion again. It was not him that we could see joining the break... He's actually given up and waited for the peloton. September 3, 2026 – 8:40 AMThe gap has just reached five minutes.September 3, 2026 – 8:43 AMBuitrago is pushing on in the front of the break, trying to whittle things down a bit.Riders like him will be hoping they can get rid of Omrzel, because that will give a smaller break a better chance of winning the stage.Van Aert, Almeida, Lutsenko, Bisiaux and Kron are with him.September 3, 2026 – 8:44 AMStill a lot of action and climbing to come today.September 3, 2026 – 8:48 AMThat early attempt to split up the break hasn't really worked, still a big group all together at the base of this long climb.September 3, 2026 – 8:50 AMBahrain are understandably taking a lot of responsibility in the break. They have KOM points and GC positions to gain.September 3, 2026 – 8:51 AMIf you're looking for something to read whilst the race is relatively calm, I spoke with Paul Seixas yesterday about his upcoming races.Paul Seixas raring to take on Canadian GPs and World Championships with Pogačar possible absence opening up opportunitiesFrench star will return from post-Tour de France break at Grand Prix Québec before big goals of Worlds and Il LombardiaSeptember 3, 2026 – 9:02 AMStill 11km left of this climb to go. It hasn't been too eventful so far.September 3, 2026 – 9:05 AMIt's deceptively calm right now. Still two really big climbs to come after this one.September 3, 2026 – 9:11 AMThe gap is up to six minutes now. How much elastic are the peloton going to give this break? At what point does it come un-closeable?With two such long climbs left, a lot can change in the finale, so six minutes definitely isn't too much to close, but I wonder what Movistar's strategy is here.September 3, 2026 – 9:20 AMWoooops Luke Tuckwell nearly crashed into a soigneur in the feed zone there. Just about avoided disaster.September 3, 2026 – 9:25 AMVan Aert and Buitrago go head to head for the points and WVA wins it again.September 3, 2026 – 9:26 AMVan Aert has 30 points in the KOM classification now, and Buitrago has 38.September 3, 2026 – 9:27 AMVan Aert and Buitrago are on their own on the descent again, just pushing on after that KOM sprint. September 3, 2026 – 9:31 AMVan Aert and Buitrago have 20 seconds on the rest of the break, and 6:40 on the peloton.September 3, 2026 – 9:32 AMEnjoying our live race coverage? Subscribe to Cyclingnews for an all-access pass to our unrivalled reporting of WorldTour racing, bike tech and exclusive in-depth features. Plus, access to the Cyclingnews app to follow the action on-the-go!September 3, 2026 – 9:33 AMI think Van Aert and Buitrago have just agreed to slow up and wait for the rest of the break to rejoin them.September 3, 2026 – 9:34 AMOur leaders have been swept back up by the break.September 3, 2026 – 9:42 AMGap is coming down ever so slightly. The road will head uphill soon, though the Alto del Velefique doesn't officially start for another 15km.September 3, 2026 – 9:46 AMThe break aren't really working that well together anymore. Some riders are committed and taking their turns but others are not quite sharing the load. September 3, 2026 – 9:47 AMElsewhere in the cycling world, stage 2 of the Tour of Britain Men just finished.September 3, 2026 – 9:49 AMMas is looking comfortable but alert in the red jersey in the peloton.September 3, 2026 – 9:52 AMThe gap is nearly seven minutes now. Still 30 riders in the front – no one has really been dropped.Movistar are riding at their own pace on the front of the bunch, not really chasing.September 3, 2026 – 9:57 AMJakob Omrzel is getting pretty close to the virtual lead now.Movistar don't seem to care that much right now – they can be confident that the gap own't be eight minutes at the end of the day – but they might think they can lure other teams into doing some work.September 3, 2026 – 10:07 AMStarting the penultimate, cat. 1 climb. There's bonus seconds at the top of this one, and the intermediate sprint is in a few kilometres.September 3, 2026 – 10:10 AMAlmeida and UAE are setting a pace here which is finally putting some riders in trouble and beginning to make the selections in this group.No trouble for Van Aert though, who takes 20 pts at the sprint.September 3, 2026 – 10:11 AMVan Aert has sat up and is now going backwards fast. Mission accomplished for him, extending his lead in green and grabbing some bonus KOM points.September 3, 2026 – 10:13 AMAlmeida is still grinding away on the front. Nearly at the top now so Buitrago is winding up to score some more points.September 3, 2026 – 10:44 AMBuitrago graps the maximum 10 points, just ahead of Lutsenko.September 3, 2026 – 10:45 AMThe GC group catches up with Castrillo from the break, so Romeo can finally pull off. Carapaz must be feeling good to try something again today.September 3, 2026 – 11:01 AMOnto the final climb we go!The first section is the steepest part.September 3, 2026 – 11:04 AMRomeo is back on the front in the GC group. What a machine.September 3, 2026 – 11:05 AMLuke Tuckwell and Jack Haig are getting dropped from the lead group. Lutsenko too.September 3, 2026 – 11:07 AMThe gap is still five minutes.Buitrago is pushing the pace in the lead. Berrade is sticking with him really well, with Bisiaux and Omrzel behind.September 3, 2026 – 11:08 AMThe French squad are winding up the pace on the front of the GC group now as they hit the hardest part of the climb.It's already making life difficult for Skjelmose and Kuss.September 3, 2026 – 11:09 AMDecathlon are riding for Giro runner-up Felix Gall, who is 1:39 behind Mas overall.September 3, 2026 – 11:10 AMCallum Scotson is setting the pace, with Riccitello and Muhlberger still there behind him so Gall has plenty of support.But as I say that, Riccitello pulls off, he can't stay with his own team. So suddenly Gall only has Muhlberger with him.September 3, 2026 – 11:11 AMIt's only Muhlberger, Gall, Mas, Onley, Roglič and Carapaz in the GC group now.They're still 4:35 down on the leaders with 13km to go, so it might not be a fight for the stage, but we'll see some GC action today.September 3, 2026 – 11:12 AMMas and Roglič are able to follow, Onley can't.September 3, 2026 – 11:13 AMUp front, Omrzel and Berrade are dropping Bisiaux after Buitrago pulled off.September 3, 2026 – 11:13 AMGall is trying to get Mas to come through for a turn. Stage win still open.September 3, 2026 – 11:17 AMHe dispatches with Berrade and leads by himself.He's riding for both a stage win and a big GC gain, both of which would be massive for the 20-year-old Slovenian.September 3, 2026 – 11:18 AMThe gap is hovering at four minutes now after initially falling.September 3, 2026 – 11:19 AMBig move from the red jersey, riding away from Roglič and Gall quickly with apparent ease. Neither had anything in response.He has a chance to really extend and solidify his GC lead here. September 3, 2026 – 11:20 AMOmrzel has 1:15 on Berrade, 3:50 on Mas.Can he hold off the red jersey to take the stage win?September 3, 2026 – 11:21 AMSeptember 3, 2026 – 11:23 AMMas catches up with García Pierna from the break, and hops onto his wheel for some help.September 3, 2026 – 11:26 AMIt's Gall who is doing all the work in the chase group, Roglič isn't really contributing.September 3, 2026 – 11:29 AMTuckwell joins Roglič in the chase. Bisiaux also comes back. So now there's a bit of an actual chase to be had.September 3, 2026 – 11:30 AMMas (with García Pierna) has just under 45 seconds on Gall and Roglič.With Tuckwell and Bisiaux there now, can he hold them off?September 3, 2026 – 11:30 AMOmrzel is on the way to victoryGarcía Pierna drops away, and Mas is still 3:40 down on Omrzel.He won't make that up in 4km – the Slovenian is going to win the stage, bar disaster.September 3, 2026 – 11:32 AMTuckwell, Bisiaux and Muhlberger are all there in the chase group as domestiques, and they are making gains on Mas.September 3, 2026 – 11:33 AMIt's steep again up the top. Omrzel looks so tired, but he's so close to such a special win.September 3, 2026 – 11:35 AMWho needs Pogačar? The Vuelta has a new Slovenian star today.Omrzel leads by 3:22 over Mas. There are remnants of the break in between the two, so Mas is't riding for second place currently.September 3, 2026 – 11:36 AMMas is holding firm with a 40 second gap, the chasers' advancements have definitely stalled.September 3, 2026 – 11:37 AMIt's bare and exposed on the top of this climb. Really atmospheric and plenty of fans have made their way up.The chasers can see Mas on these long, straight final kilometres.September 3, 2026 – 11:38 AMOmrzel is bringing it home!Muhlberger is doing the work chasing Mas, but they're not making many inroads.September 3, 2026 – 11:39 AMJakob Omrzel wins stage 12!What a HUGE result for the 20-year-old, well-earnt after a whole day in the breakaway, riding everyone off his wheel and indeed holding off none other than the race leader.We'll have to wait to see just what gains he's made in the GC.September 3, 2026 – 11:41 AMIt's not quite clear how many riders were in between Omrzel and Mas, so not sure yet if the Spaniard will take bonus points here.September 3, 2026 – 11:42 AMUrko Berrade takes second, Santiago Buitrago thirdThat's a fantastic result for Kern Pharma. And a 1-3 for Bahrain.No bonus points for Mas, but he's still gaining a lot.September 3, 2026 – 11:43 AMSeptember 3, 2026 – 11:43 AMLooks like Mas finished about 30 seconds ahead of Gall and Roglič to add to his GC lead.September 3, 2026 – 11:46 AMOnley just finished the stage, a good two minutes down on Mas.September 3, 2026 – 11:47 AMJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousUrko Berrade Fernandez (Spa) Kern PharmaSantiago Buitrago (Col) Bahrain VictoriousAlexey Lutsenko (Kaz) NSN CyclingMauri Vansevenant (Bel) Soudal Quick-StepFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostGregor Mühlberger (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMSeptember 3, 2026 – 11:48 AMA really solid day out for Mas.September 3, 2026 – 11:49 AMLove the confidence from Omrzel at the finish.I'm not surprised, because I know how much work I put in, and I knew that this day was going to come sooner or later. But for sure I was not expecting it 100% in the first Grand Tour. I still can't believe what I did, but I felt super good, I'm still feeling OK, I'm not tired. So I'm just enjoying it at the moment.September 3, 2026 – 11:52 AMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostOscar Onley (GBr) Netcompany IneosJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousMattias Skjelmose (Den) Lidl-TrekSepp Kuss (USA) Visma-Lease A BikeGregor Mühlberger (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMHarold Tejada (Col) XDS AstanaSeptember 3, 2026 – 12:04 PMCatch up with the full stage report here.Vuelta a España: Jakob Omrzel wins stage 12 as Enric Mas has another stellar ride on Calar AltoMovistar rider extends his race lead on searing daySeptember 3, 2026 – 12:08 PMMore on Onley's tough day today.Oscar Onley suffers huge dent to Vuelta a España podium hopes after early crash and summit finish strugglesNetcompany Ineos leader drops from fourth to fifth on a trying day

item.title: NBA investigation ends with LA Clippers sent 25 seasons back in time
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The NBA’s nearly year-long investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers has ended with one of the harshest punishments in league history, sending the franchise back to territory last seen during Minnesota’s Joe Smith salary-cap scandal 25 seasons ago.The League has concluded that the Clippers violated salary-cap circumvention rules by facilitating endorsement deals for Kawhi Leonard with Aspiration, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics and Lockton Insurance, as first reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania.The investigation began after reporting by Torre, and the process was conducted by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.The sanctions immediately reshape the Clippers’ already-long-gone future:The Clippers have been fined $30 million, the largest team fine in NBA history.Los Angeles is losing its first-round picks in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033.The Clippers have been placed under a five-year compliance and monitoring program.Owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended from all league and team activities for one year.President of business operations Gillian Zucker has been suspended without pay for one year.President of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been suspended without pay for six months.Leonard was fined $700,000 for improper benefits.Dennis “Uncle Dennis” Robertson has been banned from conducting business with NBA teams for five years, although Kawhi is his lone client.The scale of the punishment closely mirrors, although it clearly tops it, the NBA’s response to Minnesota in 2000. More than 25 years ago, former NBA commissioner David Stern stripped the Timberwolves of five first-round picks and fined the franchise $3.5 million after determining it had entered into an illegal secret agreement with Smith. Two of Minnesota’s five picks were later returned.The Clippers’ draft situation is particularly tough. After years of outgoing picks tied to the Paul George trade, the latest penalties leave Los Angeles of its own first-round selections under the current setup. Sheesh…The NBA suspended Ballmer for knowingly seeking to help Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities and approving a business arrangement connected to the Aspiration endorsement. Zucker was cited for being directly culpable in the endorsement arrangements and for providing false and misleading statements to investigators, while Frank was disciplined for his involvement and for approving impermissible expenses involving Leonard and his family.Funnily enough, Leonard’s punishment differed significantly from Smith’s 25 seasons earlier, as Kawhi came out pretty much unscathed. Smith’s contract was voided in 2000, while the NBA decided to leave Leonard’s contract intact and instead ordered him to pay $700,000 over improper benefits. Lots of money to us, pocket money for the Klaw.Los Angeles “vehemently” rejected the NBA’s findings and said it intends to challenge the ruling through every available avenue. Meanwhile, Kawhi is still on his way to Canada to play basketball north of the border next season.

item.title: Several current, former Knicks ball out in FIBA World Cup Qualifiers
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: I know it’s not everyone’s cup of tea, but I do really love international basketball. Really, I love all forms of national-team events. It’s the reason I watch the World Cup religiously and ignore soccer’s existence for much of the following four years. It’s why I tune in to a lot of sports I usually wouldn’t during the Olympics, both summer and winter. Basketball is no exception, except it’s a sport I do actually watch quite a lot.It’s a good thing this isn’t a big international basketball summer, as the Knicks are enjoying their offseason following their historic playoff run and third NBA championship. The next two summers, though, are full of it. The FIBA World Cup will take place in Qatar next summer and will determine who plays at the 2028 LA Olympics.You do have to qualify for that, however, which is what’s gone on this summer. Dozens of countries around the globe are taking to the court in hopes of qualifying for the FIBA World Cup, a place that these nations almost have to be at to even have a chance of calling themselves Olympians. As such, many NBA players are getting reps in this offseason overseas, particularly the Euros. Just look at Nikola Jokic and Victor Wembanyama squaring off in a heated game during a qualifer to a qualifier in the middle of the offseason:Two current Knicks and three former Knicks* competed in the most recent window of games across the world, so let’s check in on them and how they balled out for their country:Pacome Dadiet (Ivory Coast)Dadiet is a native of France; that much is true, but he was born to Ivorian immigrants along the southern coast, just outside of Nice, so he elected to represent Côte d’Ivoire (Ivory Coast). This was actually his senior national team debut after playing for France as a teenager. Ivory Coast entered the second round of qualification in a very good spot with a 5-1 record that carries over into Group F. With the window’s games being played in Dakar, Senegal, the Ivorians first squared off with Mali last Thursday, winning a narrow 83-77 result. Dadiet, playing alongside his older brother, Maxence, for the first time, had nine points and nine rebounds, going 4-for-12 from the field and 1-for-8 from three. What the Knicks will like here are the five offensive rebounds, something the team might need some help with after the departure of Mitchell Robinson.On Saturday, they faced off with Egypt and won another close contest, 72-66. Dadiet scored 13 points with six rebounds in 25 minutes, going 5-for-15 from the field and 3-for-7 from deep, while the team lost his minutes by 12 points.Ivory Coast re-took the court the next day on Sunday for a game against Angola and got blown out, losing 91-70 to conclude the August window. Dadiet had 10 points, seven assists, and five rebounds across 31 minutes, going 2-for-9 from the field and missing all four of his threes. The jumper still isn’t there right now.As with every other FIBA Qualifier, the remaining three dates will all be in the February 2027 window, meaning any NBA talent will have no control over what their country does from here. Ivory Coast sits at 7-2 and would likely only need to win one of their final three games to get to Qatar.Jose Alvarado (Puerto Rico)The only Olympian on the current Knicks’ roster, Alvarado played for his father’s country in Paris back in 2024 and continues to represent them on the international stage. Unfortunately for Alvarado, the prospects of getting back to Paris are increasingly slim.Puerto Rico advanced by the slimmest of margins in Group B with a paltry 2-4 record, which unfortunately carried over into Group F play in the second round. In the two games in the August window, where Alvarado was able to participate, they could not manage a win.The first game last Thursday against Argentina got away from them in the second half, as they lost 89-75 in Mar de Plata. Alvarado had 19 points, six rebounds, and four assists, but also committed five turnovers in 36 minutes of work, going 7-for-15 from the field and 3-for-8 from deep. As the clear focal point of the offense, he was consistently targeted.On Monday, P.R. stayed in South America, visiting Uruguay in Montevideo and losing 80-75, falling behind early and never recovering. Once again playing considerable minutes, Alvarado was held to just three points on 1-for-9 shooting, but dished out nine assists with just two turnovers in 33 minutes of action, posting a positive plus-minus.With four matchdays remaining in November and February, Puerto Rico is going to have to likely win at least three to have a shot at the FIBA World Cup, sitting at 2-6 with the Bahamas currently sitting in fourth at 4-4 as the last team in.Does Dillon Jones count as a current Knick or is he an OAKAAK? The two-time NBA champion is currently a free agent, but is a strong contender to take one of the team’s open two-way spots after participating in Summer League. Nonetheless, he’s in the gray area… for now.The state of USA Basketball is as follows. We care a lot about the Olympics; we care a bit about FIBA; we don’t give a damn about anything else. Unlike other countries, which have some of their best and brightest playing these qualifiers, Team USA is currently a smorgasbord of ex-college stars and guys with brief stints in the league. Here’s who Jones was teammates with this week. All of these would qualify as “good pulls” if you want to prove your ball knowledge:Mike James – former Brooklyn Net teammate of KD and KyrieJaron Blossomgame – 27 career games with the 2019 Cavs, All-ACC guard at ClemsonCole Swider – former Laker who split time at Syracuse and Villanova in collegeDeJon Jarreau – All-AAC guard for Houston who’s played 26 career NBA games for Memphis and IndianaKevon Harris – played 36 games for Orlando, Stephen F. Austin gradPedro Bradshaw – played college at Bellarmine and Eastern KentuckyDarius Brown II – UDFA out of Utah State who played three minutes for Cleveland on February 24thTyler Smith – 33rd pick by the Bucks in 2024, 35 career gamesGarrison Brooks – started for UNC and Mississippi State across a five-year collegiate career. Was a Knick for three days in September 2022Orlando Robinson – 115 games for four teamsI mean, look at this group.They started the August window last Thursday in Santiago against Chile, riding a Swider 19-point game to a blowout victory. Jones didn’t play much, only four minutes where he had a rebound and an assist.Four days later, on Monday, they came home to face Colombia in Washington, D.C., where they won 102-80. Jones again played only four minutes, scoring two points with a rebound and an assist.While already qualified for the Olympics by being the host country, the U.S. will want revenge after a terrible 2023 World Cup showing, so these are still important to them. With four matchdays remaining, the Americans are firmly on top with a 7-1 record, as close to clinched as possible. They won’t need any NBA talent for this.Mamadi Diakite (Guinea) – Guinea went 4-2 in Round 1 and took two of their three games in the August window, with the former Knick being a big part of them being on track to compete in Qatar next summer. He had 14-11-6 in a bad shooting game in the loss against South Sudan, but rebounded to put up 11-4-4 with five stocks in the win over Cabo Verde, while posting 12-5-5 with four stocks against Cameroon.Diakite played seven total games as a Knick in 2023-24, including four in the postseason in garbage time, as the rotating 15th roster spot. He currently plays in Dubai.Willy Hernangomez (Spain): There is no Knick from the late-2010s dark ages that I have more of a heart for than Hernangomez, who I believed in way too much. Spain went 5-1 in the first round and looked as formidable as ever entering Group E play, but have hit a major roadbump.Willy, playing alongside his brother Juancho, scored seven points with two rebounds in a 95-89 loss to Portugal to open the August window, before being held off the board in just eight minutes of play in an overtime loss to a Giannis-less Greece.

item.title: The Diawara Question: Sifting through summer league noise
item.author: John Gove
item.content:encoded: Summer League notoriously creates optical illusions. Hot shooting can spark irrational hype, while a cold stretch can trigger unnecessary panic. For Mohamed Diawara, the exhibition run landed directly into the panic bucket. Struggling to find a rhythm, the young wing looked disjointed offensively and out of sync with the game’s pace.Of course, context changes everything. Shortly after play in Las Vegas concluded, news emerged that Diawara had played through a fracture left ring finger. After successful surgery, he has already resumed on-court workouts as he prepares for training camp.Evaluating Diawara requires moving past one compromised Summer League performance. Behind the overdramatic noise is a long-limbed prospect with an intriguing foundation, organizational financial backing, and a defined set of benchmarks under Mike Brown.Diawara possesses the physical build modern front offices hope to find on the wing. His long wingspan and standing reach give him the length to shrink the floor, clog passing lanes, and effectively contest perimeter shots. Positionally, he symbolizes the length-and-versatility prototype modern NBA defense demands.During his rookie campaign, Diawara logged 69 regular-season appearances, averaging 9.2 minutes a game. While 3.6 points and 1.4 rebounds per game appear modest on paper, his underlying efficiency provides reasons for optimism. Shooting 36.9% from three, he demonstrated a reliable catch-and-shoot stroke. More importantly, he flashed against high-level competition. Against the Pelicans in December, Diawara recorded a career-high 18 points in 18 minutes, while going 4-for-4 from beyond the three-point line. Later in the season, he held his own against Jaylen Brown in Boston, demonstrating the lateral quickness necessary to stay in front of elite scorers.Signing Diawara to a four-year, $10 million contract in June, New York’s front office signaled its belief in his potential. The team-friendly deal cements his status as a long-term developmental investment instead of a player merely fighting for a roster spot. If his ball-handling and straight-line driving improve over time, his ceiling compares to the likes of Jerami Grant or a Pascal Siakam (light). If he simply masters the role of a spot-up shooting threat, he becomes a rotational wing similar to Naji Marshall or Kyle Anderson.When evaluating Diawara’s path for the upcoming season, expectation management is crucial. New York enters the season as defending champs, showcasing a deep, established veteran rotation. Charity minutes will not exist, leaving limited non-garbage-time minutes. Realistically, Diawara projects as developmental depth set to absorb low-leverage regular-season minutes. His primary function will be to serve as a low-cost insurance policy when veterans need a rest or sustain a minor injury. As he showed last season, he can effectively step into spot starts or ten-minute stints without derailing the offense. No one should expect Diawara to walk out of training camp as a consistent 15-to-20 minute staple. Instead, his job is to stay ready, refine his practice habits, and provide flexible floor spacing whenever match-ups demand extra size.For Diawara to force his way into Mike Brown’s primary rotation, three distinct areas of his game must take steps forward. First, earning Brown’s trust requires total scheme discipline and faster defensive processing. He has the physical length to switch across multiple positions, but physical tools mean little if the rotational decisions are late. Diawara must demonstrate rapid awareness and avoid blown coverages by staying disciplined against perimeter pump fakes.Second, he needs to prove he can provide high-volume floor spacing. Shooting 36.9% from deep last season established a solid foundation. However, it occurred on limited volume. To share the floor with ball-dominant creators, Diawars needs to prove his three-point efficiency holds up under higher volume and heavier defense. If defenses must respect his jumper, it stretches the floor and unlocks driving lanes.Finally, a 1.4 rebounding average over 9.2 minutes per game is insufficient for someone with Diawara’s standing reach. In Brown’s system, defensive possessions are not complete until a rebound is secured. Diawara must play with greater urgency on the glass, utilizing his frame to box out and consistently secure contested boards.Mohamed Diawara’s frustrating July was an injury-impacted blip. It was not a developmental setback. With finger surgery in the rearview and four years of contract security, his raw skill and attributes remain intriguing. His journey from an end-of-the-bench project to a steady rotation player depends entirely on how quickly his defensive processing catches up to his physical gifts. Whether his quickest path to consistent minutes lies as a mobile, small-ball power forward or strictly as a perimeter wing, it will be one of the most compelling developmental storylines.

item.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘We don’t talk about the trophy’
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: We’re already into September, and that can only mean one thing: we’re back in business.Starting today, your freshest and first Bulletin of the 2027-28 NBA season.(Here’s a small bunch of quotes, because the calendar page might have flipped but it’s not that we’re already close to anything of importance.) On putting last season’s championship behind entering their title defense:“We don’t want to speak of the trophy, we don’t talk about the trophy, we don’t want to see the trophy. We want to come in with the same mindset, if not, even a tougher mindset than we had last year… It’s important for us to come into this season to be like, ‘That’s over with.’”On modeling his early career stint in Dallas after JJ Barea:“My mindset was, I’m filling JJ Barea’s role. He came off the bench for Dallas. He did all these great things for Dallas. That’s where I see myself. I’m gonna work to be better, but that’s where I see myself. That’s where I feel like I can help this team.“The more you show in your role, the longer your leash gets, the more you’re able to do. People just want to say, ‘Hey, I can do this, I can do that.’ Well, do what’s asked of you first. Perfect it. Master it.”On refusing to call himself the “King of New York”:“I’ve never called myself the king of New York. I will never call myself the king of New York.“Imagine I get on this call with you, right? I’m like, ‘Yo, no king of New York’s here,’ whatever, whatever. You guys are going to look like, ‘What the f**k, this dude is so self-centered.’”On staying grounded as his profile has grown:“I just find a way to kind of be the same because of the people around me. I have the same people I had around since high school.”On the belief that powered the Knicks’ championship run:“Believe. That’s one thing you got to do is believe. The way we did it, 53 years, a lot of people say we were supposed to be there but still doubted us. A lot of people thought the first round was a way out because how we started. So I guess faith, believe. We just believed in each other, we believed in what we could do and that’s what made us champions.”On his goal of becoming a Sixth Man of the Year candidate:“I still haven’t done what I wanted to do with my career. I got a lot of goals that I want to push for and this is probably going to be the most hard-working summer I probably put in. I want to be in the conversation of Sixth Man of the Year one day. Obviously I got to work, obviously situations where the minutes, consistency and stuff like that is always going to be a problem because I know I’m never going to pass the eye test. If you look at me, I’m not the most tallest, most athletic to the NBA world. So I just know going into a room, I got to be the most out-working person, hardest-working person and the rest will take care of itself.”On representing the Philippines:“When you got Filipino blood, [you] take the whole country with you, the whole pride.“We’re doing a lot for the country and the culture.”On Jalen Brunson being New York’s king:“I’m happy as the mayor. Jalen Brunson is the king.”On wanting to become Team USA’s general manager:“One of my main goals is to be the GM of Team USA. In one of these Olympics, one of these years, I want to do that job one time.”On the globalization of basketball and international players becoming the NBA’s best:“Our game is global. We play basketball all around the world (…) And it’s about time. They’ve been coming into the league since the 80s. It’s just natural evolution that guys from around the world are going to assume those positions as the best players in the league.”

item.title: Red Bull signs key Aston Martin engineer as Lambiase replacement
(Late) August P&T mailbag: Best of the worst years, all-time Knicks vs. all-time Celtics & Juju Reese
item.author: Matthew Miranda
item.content:encoded: September beckons, bitches. Let’s mailbag.What would your team look like if you assembled it from the stinky years of the 2000s-2010s?In order to tackle this question, I had to settle on what exactly “2000s-2010s” meant. We talking just the awful aughts, ending with the 2009-10 season? Or the whole stinking two decades of stank? I found myself confronted by a mystery I’d never wanted to solve: who was worse, the 2000s Knicks or the 2010s Knicks?To really get the stink marinating, I compared two nine-year abominations: the Knick teams from 2002-2010 and from 2014-2022. Combined that’s 18 seasons, 17 below .500, 16 missing the playoffs. eight losses in nine playoff games and a partridge in a pear tree. Before I give you the numbers, what does your gut tell you? Which Knicks like they were worse?From 2002-2010 the Knicks were 279-459; adjusted for 82 games that’s 31-51. The 2014-2022 Knicks went 262-450, a 30-50 pace. The numbers wouldn’t settle this debate. Futility being in the eye of the beholder, I had to dig deep. Was there anything particularly sadder about one batch versus the other? For me, there is. In 2013-14, New York was coming off a tremendous run the year before, plus three consecutive winning seasons and playoff appearances. Carmelo Anthony had just led the league in scoring while finishing third for MVP. J.R. Smith was top-20 in points, Jason Kidd top-20 in steals and Tyson Chandler top-10 in offensive rebounds, an All-Star and First Team All-Defense.The writing was on the wall once Kidd retired and James Dolan strong-armed Glenn Grunwald outta town and Andrea Bargnani in, but there was reason to feel good heading into 2014. There was excitement in 2016 for the arrival of Kristaps Porziņģis. In 2019 there was hope — if not conviction — that Kevin Durant, Kyrie Irving and Zion Williamson were on their way to save the day. The 2001-02 Knicks were post-Patrick Ewing and, not coincidentally, not good, failing to win a playoff series in 2001 for the first time since 1991. Jeff Van Gundy left, Marcus Camby and a lottery pick were soon to follow in exchange for the low point of Antonio McDyess’ career, Latrell Sprewell was almost out the door and Isiah Thomas about to walk through it. .At least the 2010s Knicks had the precedent of the 2000s teams to slightly soften the blow. Watching their initial sinking into stinking, from winning 17 playoff series in 12 years (1989-2000) to winning a single playoff game the next dozen, didn’t merely cause despair. It was a disorienting fall from grace. The 2010s were a bad headache. The 2000s were that plus vertigo.Without further ado, my ‘02-’10 Knick faves: One Saturday late in my sophomore year of college, some friends and I got in on some pickup games on campus. This was the long-gone dark ages, when I was active and thin and a pretty good baller, and that day I was . The fadeaway couldn’t miss. People were calling me Jordan. It was a very small, insignificant time and place in history, and if you weren’t literally there experiencing it in real time, it makes neither sense nor difference. So it goes with those of us who swore allegiance to the Frank Williams cult twentysomething years ago — if you weren’t there, it makes zero sense. To be fair, it didn’t make a lotta sense even if you were; Williams, a point guard, shot just 35% from the field and 30% from deep and started only three games over two years in New York. And yet if the Knicks announce tomorrow they’ve signed Williams outta retirement, I’d tell Jalen Brunson thank you for your service, now get thee to the bench. The prophecy must be fulfilled.Crawford and Lee were that restaurant that used to be open near you that was delightfully, surprisingly good. It had no business being that good, and it closed years ago. But you appreciated it when it was there, and the memories still warm you today. Looking at you, Amy’s Place in Buffalo. R.I.P.Kurt Thomas I loved because he was a true warrior for righteousness, willing to tangle with anybody and everybody who was in the wrong, no matter who it was. Whether that be a future Hall of Famer.Or the biggest fish in his own pond, like in 2004 when Thomas told Knick teammate Stephon Marbury, “Everyone in this organization is afraid of you, but I’m not. I’ll beat your ass.”Thomas joins Ewing — I think — as the only Knicks who’ve impacted winning for the club over a 14-year stretch. A key reserve for the 1999 Knicks, many of us still fondly remember the final game Thomas ever played down the stretch in 2013: the Knicks had lost a season-high four straight games and five of six as they played in Utah without Carmelo. Gutting through 27 minutes, Thomas helped the Knicks snap the losing skid and kickstart a 13-game winning streak, the finishing touch on their best season in 13 years.I hold a special place in my heart for Dr. Michael Doleac because of December 30, 2002. I was driving from Rochester to New York City and a friend tagged along looking to visit a friend in Pennsylvania. My friend considered himself hilarious for not telling me the drinks he was downing the whole drive down were spiked; by the time I figured out he was drunk, he figured out we were lost. We were “near” enough that his friend came and got him, leaving without leaving me directions to get back toward the city. It was dark out in the middle of nowhere, Pennsylvania, pre-Google maps (the less said about Mapquest, the better). I spent the drive low on gas, cursing my friend for my being lost in what looked like every horror movie ever and living and dying with the back and forth in WFAN’s broadcast of what ended up a one-point Knick win over the NBA champion Spurs. In arguably his finest hour as a ‘bocker, Doleac scored 16 points (two off his Knick-high) and grabbed eight boards (tying his Knick best) against Tim Duncan and David Robinson. I wanna end this with “This doctor makes house calls,” but the game was in New York. Then again, “This doctor takes patient visits” just doesn’t work at all. Gimme your best Doleac tag line.[List your] ranking of trades/signings/moves that built the 2026 champion Knicks.16) Drafting Pacôme Dadiet15) Signing Jeremy Sochan13) Signing Mo Diawara12) Signing Ariel Hukporti11) Drafting Miles McBride10) Signing Landry Shamet9) Drafting Mitchell Robinson 8) Trading for Mikal Bridges7) Trading for Josh Hart6) Signing Jalen Brunson’s first contract5) Trading for Karl-Anthony Towns4) Trading for OG Anunoby3) Firing Tom Thibodeau & hiring Mike Brown2) Signing Jalen Brunson’s second contract1) Hiring Leon RoseClyde and Jalen in the backcourt with Willis, Patrick and Bernard up front. From my admittedly biased perspective, this starting five could match up with any all-time mythical squad the Celtics could put together.DeanJose’s five vs. Bill Russell, Larry Bird, Kevin McHale, John Havlicek and Paul Pierce — who ya got??The Wizards traded Angel Reese’s brother Julian “Juju” Reese to the Nuggets, who then released him. While he only played 13 games (10 starts) and 30.9 minutes per game, he put up respectable numbers on a tanking team (11.8 points/10.5 rebounds, including the most offensive rebounds per game since Hakeem Olajuwon at 4.2). He’s a little undersized at 6’9, 230 lbs., but seems like a decent candidate for the third-string center job. Thoughts?First, if this is Angel Reese stanning for her , I fully understand. And email me. Please. God, please email me, Angel Reese.Assuming this is really Stan KGRY, my only thoughts are that there are definitely dudes who’ve beaten that Olajuwon number from 1987 — Dennis Rodman did a half-dozen times by himself — and that whatever downgrade there is between Mitch and Drummond, the Knicks are probably looking to make that up with an upgrade over Hukporti. You can’t count on KAT playing heavy minutes for 82 games followed by a two-month title defense, nor do I think they want to count on Drummond being the best next man up that whole time. There is 100% room for Juju Reese to make a home and career in the NBA. I don’t see it this year in New York, though.That’s all she wrote for the mailbag, and it’s gonna be all she wrote for a while. I’m now writing about the Knicks at OnSI, and no longer at P&T. I’ve left before and returned; this feels less like “Goodbye” than “Later.” I’ll still pop into the comments sometimes, and have a few other pots starting to boil. Email if you want. I’m on Bluesky. I love you all. Not all. But you, reading this now, I love. Yes, you.

item.title: Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United return feels like a marriage of convenience | Will Unwin
item.author: Will Unwin at Old Trafford
item.content:encoded: A lack of offers and problems in finding a replacement may be behind the move, but that does not mean it cannot workThe first chant of the match was for Marcus Rashford, Manchester United’s returning rogue son, the one banished for 18 months, first to the Midlands and then Catalonia. Every football fan loves an academy product who has risen up the ranks, from scrawny child to getting 76,000 off their seats. Rashford is one of these, living out the dream of everyone inside Old Trafford and they are willing to forgive but want something in return.Not since 7 December 2024 has Rashford been seen in red at Old Trafford. Then it was as a substitute forlornly trying to turn things around in an eventual 3-2 defeat by Nottingham Forest. His relationship with Ruben Amorim was already deteriorating, the second head coach to have become irritated with Rashford. After loans with Aston Villa and Barcelona, everyone is surprised to see him back; it feels like a marriage of convenience because of a lack of offers and securing a replacement was deemed complex.Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.author: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Liverpool need midfield nous, Michael Carrick is already under pressure and Villa can bid farewell to Enzi KonsaEnzo Maresca has a shiny new £85m midfielder he could select for a debut but he may want Ayyoub Bouaddi, at 18 years old, to have a bit of time watching on from the bench to learn about the Premier League from his elders. The Moroccan may not have expected one of those to be a centre-back by trade. Marc Guéhi will be eager to make a triumphant return to Crystal Palace and may well have the opportunity to do so from central midfield, where he played last weekend in the victory over Bournemouth, scoring the equaliser. The centre-back was a surprise selection in the blocker role next to Elliot Anderson, but equipped himself admirably and was not limited to the dirty work, often being found in more advanced positions in open play and happy to have the ball at his feet. His long-term future is unlikely to be outside defence but further proof of Guéhi’s adaptability will be a positive for Maresca, as a long season awaits. Crystal Palace v Manchester City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)Liverpool v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 12.30pmBournemouth v Everton, Saturday 3pmCoventry v Hull, Saturday 3pmTottenham v Newcastle, Saturday 5.30pmContinue reading...
